transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. I guess what brings me in is... well, things are getting pretty bad at work. I'm a construction manager, and I can start a safety briefing or sit down for a plan review, trying my absolute hardest to pay attention. But within just a few minutes, my mind is completely off on three other job problems. I just drift off. And because of that, I end up missing things—important details that I know I should have caught.
Did you have trouble paying attention like this when you were a child?

Yeah, definitely. I mean, back in elementary school, my teachers were already telling my parents about it. They'd say I couldn't stay in my seat and that I talked out of turn a lot. I was always losing my homework, too. And I'd just... rush right through directions before I even really understood what I was supposed to be doing.
Do these attention problems also happen in other parts of your life besides work?

Yeah, it's definitely happening at home, too. My wife is just... she's really worn down at this point from constantly having to remind me about things I told her I would handle. It's really frustrating for her. 

And to be honest, the work stuff I mentioned earlier? It's gotten bad enough that my employer actually brought it up as a formal concern recently. There were just too many missed follow-ups and my site coordination was poorly organized. So, yeah, it's causing real problems in both places.
